name.description: The name/title of the custom move.

kind.description: Which of the three kinds of custom move this is (MC Toolkit p. 134).

template.description: The MC Toolkit template this move was written from, kept for the record.

trigger.description: The condition that fires the move, written in the books' 'when you...' form. This is the one field no custom move can do without: a move with no trigger never fires. Supports inline Markdown.
examples: When you try to get into the castle grounds of the Sleeping Beauty,
When you spend a day in the war-torn city,

impact.description: How hard the move hits, on the one-to-three star scale the MC Toolkit prints beside each template.

roll.description: The roll the move calls for. Most custom moves are diceless and leave this out.

label.description: What a `custom` stat rolls against, written as the move names it. Ignored for the three named stats.
examples: the tier of the city's {war-torn} status
the number of clues the crew has gathered

modifier.description: A flat bonus or penalty the move applies on top of the stat.

outcomes.description: What the move produces, from zero to four tiers. A diceless move carries a single untiered outcome; a rolled move carries one per tier it distinguishes.

text.description: What happens at this tier, written as the books write it. Supports inline Markdown.
examples: you get through, but you first take {entangled-3}.
the MC chooses two from the list below.

options.description: The list a tier chooses from, when its text says 'choose two from the list below'. Leave it out for an outcome that resolves in one line.

items.description: One option the tier's text points at.

pick_count.description: How many entries of `options` this tier takes. The same list often serves several tiers with a different count each, which is why the count sits on the tier and not on the list.

items.description: One result of the move, tied to the tier of the roll that produces it.

frequency.description: How often the move can fire, when the move limits itself. Prose rather than a count, because the books phrase it as fiction.

mc_note.description: An MC-facing aside: how to pitch the move at the table, what it is for, what it should not become. Supports inline Markdown.
examples: Use this to make the castle feel alive rather than to punish the players.

meta.description: Attribution and cataloging fields for the custom move's origin.

publication_type.description: Classifies the move's source to aid cataloging and tooling.

source.description: Source title (book, supplement, PDF) where this move appears.

authors.description: List of credited authors or contributors.

page.description: Page number (if relevant to the source).

description: City of Mist - a standalone custom move: a condition plus its outcomes, written for a Danger, a situation or a theme improvement. Distinct from the `custom_moves` nested in a Danger profile, which squash trigger and outcome into one description string; this target keeps them apart so a move can be printed, rolled and improved on its own.
